no_alerts_found: No alerts found during the evaluation. This happens when rule condition is unsatisfied. You may adjust the rule threshold and retry.
repeat_notifications_desc: Send periodic notifications while the alert condition remains active.
repeat_notifications_tooltip: Continue sending periodic notifications while the alert condition persists. Useful for ensuring critical alerts aren't missed during long-running incidents. Configure how often to repeat and under what conditions.
notification_message_tooltip: Customize the message content sent in alert notifications. Template variables like {{alertname}}, {{value}}, and {{threshold}} will be replaced with actual values when the alert fires.
notification_message_desc: Custom message content for alert notifications. Use template variables to include dynamic information.
notification_message_placeholder: This alert is fired when the defined metric (current value: {{$value}}) crosses the threshold ({{$threshold}})
group_alerts_tooltip: Group similar alerts together to reduce notification volume. Leave empty to combine all matching alerts into one notification without grouping.
combine_alerts_same_fields: Combine alerts with the same field values into a single notification.
add_group_by_tooltip: Add 'Group by' fields to your query to enable alert grouping
all_grouping_disabled: All = grouping of alerts is disabled
alerts_grouped_by: Alerts with same {{field}} will be grouped
empty_combined_notification: Empty = all matching alerts combined into one notification
alert_when_data_stops_desc: Send notification if no data is received for a specified time period.
alert_when_data_stops_tooltip: Useful for monitoring data pipelines or services that should continuously send data. For example, alert if no logs are received for 10 minutes
minimum_data_required_desc: Only trigger alert when there are enough data points to make a reliable decision.
minimum_data_required_tooltip: Prevents false alarms when there's insufficient data. For example, require at least 5 data points before checking if CPU usage is above 80%.
evaluation_cadence_tooltip: Controls how frequently the alert evaluates your conditions. For most alerts, 1-5 minutes is sufficient.
ask_admin_to_create: Please ask your admin to create one.
threshold_channel_required: Please select at least one channel for each threshold or enable routing policies
threshold_label_required: Please enter a label for each threshold
threshold_tab_tooltip: An alert is triggered when the metric crosses a threshold.
anomaly_tab_tooltip: An alert is triggered whenever the metric deviates from an expected pattern.
how_frequently_check_desc: How frequently this alert checks your data. Default: Every 1 minute
eval_current_month_starting_from: Current month, starting from day {{number}} at {{time}} ({{timezone}})
cumulative_window_example_hour: An hourly cumulative window for error count alerts when errors exceed 100. Starting at the top of the hour, it tracks: 20 errors by :15, 55 by :30, 105 by :45 (alert fires).
cumulative_window_example_day: A daily cumulative window for sales alerts when total revenue exceeds $10,000. Starting at midnight, it tracks: $2,000 by 9 AM, $5,500 by noon, $11,000 by 3 PM (alert fires).
cumulative_window_example_month: A monthly cumulative window for expense alerts when spending exceeds $50,000. Starting on the 1st, it tracks: $15,000 by the 7th, $32,000 by the 15th, $51,000 by the 22nd (alert fires).
cumulative_window_description:
Monitors data accumulated since a fixed starting point. The window grows over time, keeping all historical data from the start.

Example: {{example}}
rolling_window_description:
Monitors data over a fixed time period that moves forward continuously.

Example: A {{timeWindow}} rolling window for error rate alerts with 1 minute evaluation cadence. Unlike fixed windows, this checks continuously: {{examples}}, etc.
